decisions.quote: We were able to replicate the effect of age on empathy and compassion reported by Reiter et al . [ 62 ]—revealing a preservation of empathy and enhancement of compassion in OA. Concerning ToM we replicated the effect of age on ToM accuracy—showing a decline in ToM performance in OA compared with YA. Age differences with respect of ToM are of notable interest given comparable educational attainment levels in YA and OA in the current sample (coherent with Reiter et al .’s sample [ 62 ]). This speaks against the notion proposed by several authors [ 85 , 86 ] that age differences in perspective taking are mediated through differing educational levels in these cohorts. However, we did not replicate the effect of age on ToM reaction time.
decisions.reason: While the abstract broadly summarizes the directional pattern of preserved socio-affective and declining socio-cognitive processes, the discussion characterizes the replication as having 'mainly succeeded' and explicitly states in the synthesis that the effect of age on empathy, compassion, and ToM accuracy replicated whereas the effect of age on ToM reaction time (the question type by age group interaction) did not replicate. Under the codebook rules, when a replication explicitly contrasts a tested finding that failed to replicate alongside findings that replicated without an unqualified overall success verdict, the outcome is mixed.
